sandbox.summary: The patch was applied in an isolated Docker container and pytest was run. Exit code was 0. Two tests were collected (test_math_utils.py::test_add and test_math_utils.py::test_multiply) and both passed with no failures, errors, skips, or warnings. Verdict: PASS. Caveat: the suite is small (2 tests), so this confirms no regressions in the covered behavior (add and multiply) but says nothing about untested code paths.

patch.explanation: multiply() in sample-app/math_utils.py was a copy-paste of add() and used the + operator, so multiply(2, 4) returned 6 instead of 8 and test_multiply failed. Changing the operator to * makes multiply return the correct product, which satisfies both assertions in test_multiply (2*4 == 8, 3*3 == 9). The test and the add() function are untouched, so this is the only change needed.
